body.x: QuantumCat Co., Ltd. (CEO Shin-hyun Kang) participated in the 'Startup Zone' at the Eureka Park K-STARTUP integrated hall of 'CES 2023' in Las Vegas, USA from January 5 (Thursday) to 8 (Sunday, local time) for a total of 4 days.

QuantumCat is a Korean company that leads the commercialization of ‘gold nanocatalyst’, a new concept catalyst that exhibits very high catalytic activity at room temperature. This is a technical material that can effectively remove harmful or greenhouse gases, such as carbon monoxide, volatile organic compounds, and methane, without additional energy consumption or equipment, and is drawing attention as a key material for carbon neutrality in the future.

Platinum group metal catalysts, which are currently used in the global industry, require a high temperature environment exceeding 200℃ to exhibit activation, and it requires the use of more fossil fuels to create such an environment. On the other hand, QuantumCat’s gold nanocatalyst exhibits static catalytic performance even at room temperature and is characterized by its ability to effectively reduce the use of fossil fuels to raise temperatures. In addition, the fact that these characteristics have additional effects of preventing serious accidents and respiratory diseases caused by harmful gases is also emphasized.

Applying their differentiated new material-based catalyst, QuantumCat is known to have completed a filter prototype and is conducting continuous PoC with large corporations in Korea and overseas operating air purifier businesses. They have finished proving the effectiveness of the product in the actual environment of use with various tests. The company explained that they submitted it to the trade show for exhibition and expects this to lead to actual sales results.

An official of QuantumCat explained that, “With the application of low-carbon green growth and carbon neutrality policies spreading around the world, ultimately, the main agendas to achieve these goals are reduction of fossil fuel use, use of alternate energy, improvement of energy efficiency processes, and CCUS, which all require catalyst technology at the core,” and said, “Our new concept catalyst technology developed with our company’s own technology is projected to become a core technology that supports the sustainability of humanity through carbon neutrality.”

Furthermore, they revealed that the company is investing their capabilities in basic research for full-scale commercialization. The official said, “The biggest hurdle in utilizing metal nanoparticles as catalysts was imparting stability to the nanoparticles,” and said that, “Our company was able to overcome this through ‘nano cage’ technology, and is using this to conduct basic research for the commercialization of metal and non-metal nanocatalysts.”

‘CES’ is the world’s biggest IT trade show and is a place where one can see the direction and trends of the appliance industry of the entire world. Hosted by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), it is held annually in Las Vegas, USA in January. Having reported on CES for 17 consecutive years, AVING News started reporting news of CES to the entire world since 2006, and conducted ‘BEST OF CES’, which chose the most innovative product and technology, and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA, which chose the best innovative company in Korea. In addition, it vividly relayed on-site issues in CES through ‘AVING LIVE’.

The K-STARTUP Joint Pavilion featured joint participation of institutions like the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development, Seoul Business Agency, and Seoul Digital Foundation, as well as 51 Korean innovative companies, to enter the US market and discover global partners. In addition, university student supporters of CES 2023 chosen by each university (Kyunghee, Kookmin, Sogang, Chung-Ang) matched to participating companies based on their respective majors and fields of business.
